newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goodman says no near-term acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goodman says no near-term acquisitions.

text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Friday that it would be another year to 18 months before the food group would begin to consider acquisitions or sales.
Managing director David Hearn said the company's task in hand was to generate increased returns from its current assets.
"I think we have got another year or 18 months of solid work to do," Hearn told reporters after the annual meeting.
"We are saying that our task at hand at the moment is to optimise the portfolio we have," he said.
"That means we are not primarily looking to sell businesses, nor are we primarily looking to buy them."
Hearn said Goodman would respond if it received any "fabulous" offers, but said the company had had no recent offers for any of its businesses.
He believed the company would be able to make a "significant strategic move" in two years' time if it wanted to.
"We will not be limited in our strategy by our financial capability," he said.
"We have got to find the option and make it work," he said.
Hearn said there were no on-going talks about the merger of Goodman's Australian milling and baking businesses with Bunge Australia, which is owned by the Latin American Bunge group.
"We like the Bunge deal in conceptual terms, we just didn't like the financials," he said.
Goodman withdrew from the proposed merger in May.
Hearn said the gearing level would come down a little from its current 56.2 percent, but he believed interest cover was a better measure of a company's ability to afford its debt.

"We've now got interest cover of over five times and that's a very comfortable number for a business with our earnings," he said. Goodman reported earlier that interest cover had risen from 4.9 times last year to 5.6 times.
